inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: The Pain transmission text (book 235, bottom half) — the nociceptive pain definition with the TRPV transduction cascade and the Aδ/C fiber fork, the four-process blocker-list table, and the neuropathic pain block
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: PURE TEXT, THREE BLOCKS + A BULLETED LIST (pdfimages: zero raster images; the VLM census RAN this session — glm-4.6v on the 120-DPI and 200-DPI renders, staging-ph11/vlm-census.txt — confirming no figures, photographs, icons, or margin notes/mnemonics anywhere on the page): [1] the NOCICEPTIVE PAIN block — 'Pain signals transmitted to the CNS in response to mechanical, thermal, or chemical stimuli. Transient receptor potential vanilloid ligand receptors cause Ca2+ influx–induced Na+ channel activation. Signals transmitted by Aδ fibers (sharp, acute pain) or C fibers (dull, throbbing, chronic pain).' — [2] the lead-in 'Processes involved in pain transmission:' with FOUR square-bulleted rows (process names in bold): '▘ Transduction—blocked by local anesthetics, α2-agonists, gabapentinoids, NSAIDs, acetaminophen, glucocorticoids' / '▘ Transmission—blocked by local anesthetics, α2-agonists, opioids' / '▘ Modulation—blocked by TCAs, SSRIs, SNRIs, gabapentinoids' / '▘ Perception—blocked by α2-agonists, opioids, TCAs, SSRIs, SNRIs' — and [3] the NEUROPATHIC PAIN block — 'Caused by neuronal dysfunction of the CNS or PNS. Transmitted via upregulation and persistent activation of voltage-gated Na+ channels. Example: diabetic peripheral neuropathy.' No figures, margin notes, or mnemonics print in the Pain-transmission half.
inventory.kypLocation: the registry visual (PainTransmissionMap in visuals/pharm-p11.tsx — the PERIPHERY panel with the TRPV transducer glyph: stimulus chips, vanilloid ligand receptor, Ca2+ influx arrow, Na+ channel activation spark, the signal-born zigzag; the Aδ fast lane and C slow lane fork into the CNS panel with the MODULATION and PERCEPTION boxes; the four station cards with every printed blocker chip docked beneath its station and the 6·3·4·5 count chips; the NEUROPATHIC PAIN panel with the upregulated-channel nerve glyph, NO STIMULUS NEEDED flag, and the diabetic peripheral neuropathy example card; and the drug-class × station overlap ledger); the printed text is also carried verbatim in the note's table block (blocks[1]), core.what, and recall[0]/[2-6]
